compiled_state.description:
Sibling of bug 3d57-602f-0b75-48ee (found in its Step-7 construct sweep): the completion child-closure gate pays a full-store scan per child (and up to 4 with legacy fingerprint retries) when closing a container.

Mechanism: src/rebar/llm/completion_child_gate.py:82-110 loops a parent's direct children and calls compute_validity(sig, c, "completion-verifier") per child; the completion branch (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:568-574) recomputes current_material_fingerprint (1 full-store reduce via relation_snapshot.live_material_children -> _reads.list_tickets(parent=...)) and on mismatch tries _legacy_material_ok (3 more full computations). A container close with N children costs O(N)..O(4N) full-store scans.

Bug 3d57's fix added relation_snapshot.material_child_index() — a ContextVar-scoped, lazily-built, idempotent (outer-wins) child-index snapshot; live_material_children answers from it while active. It is opened inside derive_plan_material_pin_health and plan_review_health, so plan-review pin loops are covered — but the completion_child_gate loop reaches the fingerprint OUTSIDE any snapshot.

Proposed fix (small): open `with material_child_index(repo_root=repo_root):` around the child loop in completion_child_gate.py (both the gate loop at ~:82 and the evidence-block enumeration at ~:175 if it fingerprints). One scan per close instead of O(4N). Correctness precedent: the snapshot's fast path filters through counts_as_plan_material_child, byte-identical to the slow path (proven in bug 3d57; regression test tests/unit/test_pin_health_store_scan_count.py shows the counting pattern to reuse).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Full-store reduce count during a container close's child-closure check does not grow with child count (counting-seam test like test_pin_health_store_scan_count.py).
- [ ] Gate verdicts (blocking/uncertified sets) byte-identical before/after on a fixture store.
- [ ] make lint + typecheck + complexity ratchet clean.
compiled_state.title: completion child gate scans full store per child
